messages:
sherman: heads up, after the kv-prefetch flag flip we saw triton take a weird path vs cutlass on seq64 workloads — p95 jumped ~30ms for small batches. anyone else seeing this?
alyssa: saw a blip on staging last night, thought it was noise. which flag exactly?
maria: that was the `--kv-prefetch=aggressive` toggle?
sherman: yep. on H100. routing telemetry shows more fallbacks to triton kernel when prefetch moves KV-cache warms earlier.
tushar: can you paste the routing snippet or perf numbers?
sherman: here are simplified traces from the probe run (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-17T22:08:03Z] request id=abc seq=64 batch=1 -> selected=triton_fast_attn path_latency_ms=12 kv_hit=false
[2026-03-17T22:08:03Z] probe decision: prefer_triton=true reason=kv_prefetch_warm
[2026-03-17T22:08:03Z] kernel exec triton_fast_attn latency_ms=40 (vs expected 10)
[2026-03-17T22:08:03Z] fallback invoked -> cutlass_gemm path_latency_ms=15
```
sherman: note the triton kernel inflated to 40ms on hotpath, likely due to tensor layout or extra syncing after prefetch. cutlass returns faster in these runs.
maria: interesting — could be that prefetch changes memory residency and triggers uncached cuda kernels in triton, increasing register pressure.
kevin: i dug into the autotuner logs, stack shows triton relying on a different kernel variant when `kv_fragment_count>1`. attaching excerpt: 
```
autotune: model=redwood-7b variant=triton_v2 selected_score=0.72 fallback_score=0.68 reason=kv_frag>1
```
ci-bot: autotune-run #642 completed: latency_regression=+28ms for seq=64, batch=1; note=kv-prefetch enabled
tushar: can we reproduce with a microbenchmark that toggles kv-prefetch and simulates small-batch seq64? if yes we should add a gating check before flipping to aggressive.
kevin: agree. mitigation: add hysteresis in routing decider — require 3 consecutive probes showing cutlass better before switching away from triton. reduces oscillation.
alyssa: also can we try delaying prefetch slightly (50-100us) for seq<=64? maybe avoid the premature residency change.
sherman: good suggestions. i'll run a focused microbench: two runs (prefetch=off, prefetch=aggressive) with probe sampling 5000 requests and produce per-kernel histograms. i'll post results.
maria: if that reproduces, we should update the autotune objective to include a small-batch penalty so triton variants don't get chosen purely by warmup heuristics.
kevin: ping me on the run, i'll prepare a canary with hysteresis flag.
sherman: thanks — kicking off now. will post logs: `curl -X POST https://perf-run.internal/run -d '{"suite":"kv-prefetch-seq64"}'`
alyssa: :thumbsup: schedule a 9am sync if we have regression confirmed
sherman: noted, will update by 2075554980 with initial histograms.
